newsitem.title: USA: Groups urge U.S. to press Suharto on human rights.
newsitem.headline: Groups urge U.S. to press Suharto on human rights.

text.p: Nine U.S. environmental and human rights groups urged Vice President Al Gore to protest to the Indonesian government against its threat to clamp down on local environmentalists, according to a letter released on Thursday.

"We are writing to urge that you relay a message of extreme concern from the United States to Indonesian President Suharto regarding what appears to be a planned repression of Indonesian environmentalists," the groups said in a November 20 letter to Gore, an avowed environmentalist.
The letter came ahead of next week's Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Manila, which President Bill Clinton and Suharto were planning to attend.
The complaint stemmed from press reports that the Indonesian government vowed this month to crack down on any group which it considered a threat, including the Indonesian Environmental Forum (WALHI).
WALHI protested the operations of the Grasberg Copper and Gold mine in Irian Jaya, run by New Orleans-based Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc.

The Clinton administration last year moved to cut the company off from political risk insurance for the project and earlier this year reached a settlement with the company which included setting up a $100 million environmental fund for reclamation at the mine site, a spokeswoman for the Overseas Private Investment Corp said.

"Should the harassment of WALHI succeed in silencing its voice, it will send a devastating signal to citizens throughout the developing world that the United States will not stand by civic organisations whose views and democratic methods we claim to support," the groups, including Sierra Club and Amnesty International USA, told Gore.
